claude.performance_metric: JV stake exit: sold 36.5% consumer-JV stake to GSK for USD 13.0bn on June 1, 2018 (~39 months post-close)
claude.rationale: Section 2 T5 states each acquirer took over the commercial/operational base for its acquired portfolio and Novartis leveraged its Oncology R&D/commercial capabilities, so product (T4) and its processes (T5) moved together — no product-vs-process mismatch at closing (gap_45=0). Section 2 T6 documents that associated people transferred with the business alongside those processes, with retention flagged only as a prospective risk, so no realized process-vs-organization mismatch at closing (gap_56=0). Section 4 states no realized P4 product-process disruption is evidenced (p4_pathway=0) and that key-personnel retention was a forward-looking risk with no documented realized fracture (p5_pathway=0).

gemini.performance_metric: sale of its 36.5% stake in the consumer-healthcare JV to GSK for USD 13.0 billion
gemini.rationale: The dossier documents that the oncology and vaccines products transferred alongside their commercial and operational bases, with no structural gap at closing (gap_45 = 0). Key personnel transferred with the business, aligning operations and organization (gap_56 = 0). Post-deal, each acquirer successfully absorbed the products and processes without documented disruption (p4_pathway = 0), and despite forward-looking retention risks, no process-organization fracture materialized (p5_pathway = 0).

grok.performance_metric: sold 36.5% JV stake for USD 13.0 billion after ~39 months
grok.rationale: Section 2 states T4 swapped both directions and T5 'transferred with the products' while T6 'transferred with the business', directly yielding gap_45=0 and gap_56=0. Sections 3-4 explicitly state 'none documented' for P4 and P5 realized failures and note successful 2018 JV exit per pre-agreed terms.
